definitions.explanation: The introductory section at the beginning of a book, typically written by the author or another person.

examples.japanese: {序文|じょぶん}を{読|よ}んでから{本文|ほんぶん}に{進|すす}んだ。
examples.english: I read the preface before proceeding to the main text.

examples.japanese: {著者|ちょしゃ}が{序文|じょぶん}で{執筆|しっぴつ}の{動機|どうき}を{語|かた}っている。
examples.english: The author talks about the motivation for writing in the preface.

examples.japanese: {有名|ゆうめい}な{教授|きょうじゅ}が{序文|じょぶん}を{書|か}いた。
examples.english: A famous professor wrote the foreword.

notes:
USAGE: {序文|じょぶん} is used for academic books, novels, and other written works.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{序文|じょぶん}を{書|か}く (to write a preface)
・{序文|じょぶん}を{読|よ}む (to read the preface)

BOOK STRUCTURE TERMS:
・{序文|じょぶん} / まえがき - preface, foreword
・{目次|もくじ} - table of contents
・{本文|ほんぶん} - main text
・{付録|ふろく} - appendix
・あとがき - afterword

SIMILAR TERMS:
・まえがき - preface (less formal than {序文|じょぶん})
・はじめに - introduction (common in non-fiction)
・{緒言|しょげん} - preface (formal, academic)
